corrections.original: Jackel-Vapnik bet: Jackel bet 'a math theory explaining why neural networks work' by 2000; Vapnik bet 'nobody would use neural nets' by 2005; dated 1995 'by implication'
corrections.fix: Transcribed from the signed document (each signature dated 3/14/95). Bet 1: 'Jackel bets (one fancy dinner) that by March 14, 2000, people will understand quantitatively why big neural nets working on large databases are not so bad. (Understanding means that there will be clear conditions and bounds)'. Bet 2: 'Vapnik bets (one fancy dinner) that by March 14, 2005, no one in his right mind will use neural nets that are essentially like those used in 1995.' Signatures from top to bottom: V. Vapnik, L. Jackel, 'Witnessed by Y. LeCun'. Outcomes (Jackel lost 1, Vapnik lost 2) remain secondary.

corrections.original: Check reader read 'more than 10%' / 'over 10%' of US checks (Bottou Wikipedia, arXiv 1412.8341, ACM profile)
corrections.fix: Use LeCun's own words: 'reads an estimated 10 percent of all the checks written in the US' (homepage) and 'between 10 and 20% of all the checks in the US in the early 2000s' (bio). Safe narration: 'an estimated one in ten US checks'. arXiv 1412.8341 is an astrophysics master's thesis and was dropped; the Bottou Wikipedia line is uncited.

corrections.original: Bengio 2003: best MLP 252 on Brown and 109 on AP 'against modified Kneser-Ney at 117'
corrections.fix: Brown: MLP10 (mixed with an interpolated trigram) at 252 vs 312 for the best n-gram (class-based back-off, 500 classes); KN back-off 321-323. AP News: 109 vs 117 for the modified KN back-off 5-gram. '24%' is the n-gram's perplexity above the network's (312/252); the network is about 19% lower. The 24%/8% phrase and 'approximately three weeks with 40 CPUs' are verbatim.

corrections.original: Pearl's 1988 book is 'the founding text of Bayesian networks' / 'founded Bayesian networks'
corrections.fix: Pearl coined 'Bayesian network' in a 1985 paper (UCLA TR CSD-850017); the 1988 book consolidated the field and established it as a field of study. The Turing citation ('a calculus for probabilistic and causal reasoning', 2011 award) is confirmed.

corrections.original: LeCun 1989: 'A companion NIPS paper reported a 1% error rate at about a 9% reject rate' (implicitly the 1989 result)
corrections.fix: The Neural Computation 1989 paper reports 5.0% raw test error (102 mistakes) and 12.1% rejection for 1% error (SUN-4/260, SN simulator). The 9% reject figure comes only from the NIPS companion paper, which used a superset database with printed digits. The 9,298 / Buffalo NY / 7,291 / 2,007 / Holmdel claims are confirmed from the paper text.

corrections.original: LeCun joined Bell Labs in Oct 1988
corrections.fix: The year 1988 is confirmed; the month is not, so the dossier now gives the year only.

corrections.original: Bell Labs Holmdel: 'a water tower shaped like a transistor'
corrections.fix: The 127-ft white saucer-shaped tower stands on three legs. The transistor resemblance is an urban legend with no documented evidence; do not narrate it as fact. The mirrored Saarinen building ('the biggest mirror ever') is confirmed.

corrections.original: Deep Blue: 'there was no audience in the game room'; 'hand-tuned evaluation'
corrections.fix: There was no paying audience in the 35th-floor game room, but one account says 'only a few dozen VIPs were allowed in the room'. Evaluation parameters 'were determined by analyzing thousands of master games'. Wikipedia gives 30 processors and IBM gives 32. 3.5-2.5 on 11 May 1997, 19 moves, 480 chips and 200M positions/sec are all confirmed.

corrections.original: Belief section: quotation marks around 'a math theory explaining why neural networks work' (bet)
corrections.fix: This was a blog paraphrase presented as a quote. It is replaced with the verbatim bet text.

corrections.original: Schmidhuber's 'one of the most important documents in the history of machine learning' cited to [S16] (Wikipedia pages)
corrections.fix: The phrase is not on the cited Wikipedia pages. It is verified on Schmidhuber's 'Annotated History of Modern AI and Deep Learning' and 'Miraculous Year 1990-1991' pages; re-cited to S55.

corrections.original: Toronto Star (source S15): 'In 2006, Hinton and a PhD student, Ruslan Salakhutdinov, published two papers'
corrections.fix: Flagged as an error in the source: the 2006 papers are Hinton, Osindero & Teh (Neural Computation 18(7):1527-1554) and Hinton & Salakhutdinov (Science 313(5786):504-507, 28 July 2006). Do not repeat the Star's framing.

corrections.original: Jelinek: 'Whenever I fire a linguist our system performance improves' (Dec 1988, Wayne PA)
corrections.fix: This exact wording, venue and date are VERIFIED-PRIMARY as Jelinek's own recollection in his LREC 28 May 2004 slides ('The Quote'). The quip is not in the 1988 proceedings, and Moore dates a variant to 1985. On screen, attribute it as 'as Jelinek himself later recalled it'.

corrections.original: CVPR 2012 rejection 'shows the anti-neural-net attitude persisted in vision until about 2012'; LeCun wrote 'an angry letter'
corrections.fix: The rejection of Farabet et al., the letter to PC chair Serge Belongie and the ICML 2012 acceptance are confirmed (secondary). But two deep-learning face papers were accepted at CVPR 2012, and the blogger later said 'I wrote the post as a joke' and that reviewers lacked a benchmark for scene parsing. 'Angry' is not verified.

corrections.original: Bengio: neural networks 'fell out of fashion in the mid-90s' [S42]
corrections.fix: The O'Reilly page was inaccessible (Access Denied). Do not use as a quote.

corrections.original: ACM Turing profile says 'more than 10%' of checks
corrections.fix: The ACM site blocked access. Use LeCun's own 'estimated 10 percent' instead.

corrections.original: Corinna Cortes is a long-distance runner
corrections.fix: No source found; do not state it. Her role as VP at Google Research NY is confirmed.

corrections.original: Viola-Jones 'became the standard way cameras found faces in the 2000s'
corrections.fix: Paper metadata confirmed (CVPR 2001, Kauai, vol. 1 pp. I-511-I-518); the adoption claim is unverified, so do not state it.

corrections.original: IBM Watson Research Center: 'fieldstone-and-glass' curving building
corrections.fix: Saarinen's crescent-shaped, three-level building (1956-61) with windowless offices is confirmed; 'fieldstone' is not.
The letter is only linked from the blog; its tone was not checked. Describe it neutrally.

confirmed_highlights: Breiman 2001 quotes Q1-Q5 and the 5.1% vs 6.2% ZIP-code result are verbatim, including the 'then neural nets' typo (Statistical Science 16(3), Aug 2001); Random Forests is MLJ 45(1):5-32, Oct 2001
Toronto Star 17 Apr 2015: Bengio 'It was the worst possible time,' and LeCun 'We were outcast a little bit ... we couldn't get our papers published.' are verbatim
IEEE Spectrum 18 Feb 2015 (Lee Gomes): 'the so-called "Deep Learning conspiracy"', 'Neural Net Winter', 'ironclad theory'
LeCun et al. 1998 abstract: 'It is deployed commercially and reads several million checks per day'; fielded 'since June 1996' (now primary); note that the intro says 'millions of checks per month'
MNIST: 60k/10k; SD-3 Census Bureau employees and SD-1 high-school students; LeNet-5 0.95, boosted LeNet-4 0.7, SVM 1.4, linear 12.0
Cortes & Vapnik MLJ 20(3):273-297, Sept 1995; Freund & Schapire LNCS 904 pp. 23-37 (1995), JCSS 55(1):119-139 (Aug 1997), Godel Prize 2003

LSTM Neural Computation 9(8):1735-1780 (Nov 1997), abstract 'in excess of 1000 discrete-time steps'; Bengio, Simard & Frasconi IEEE TNN 5(2):157-166 (Mar 1994); Hochreiter's 1991 TU Munich diploma thesis
CIFAR NCAP 2004, proposed by Hinton with Bengio, Fleet and others; Hinton director 2004-2013
Netflix Prize: launched 2 Oct 2006; 100,480,507 ratings; tie at 10.06% (RMSE 0.8567); 20 minutes; winner named 18 Sept, award ceremony 21 Sept 2009; Commendo affiliation
Boser, Guyon & Vapnik COLT 1992 pp. 144-152; Gers et al. 2000 forget gate; Tangora 5,000 words; Vapnik dates (ICS 1961-1990, Bell Labs from end of 1990, NEC 2002)
